findings.explanation: The three root gitlinks are inside the project. Following data/raw_eyegaze exposes an absolute author-local source URL, supporting partial transitive closure. This does not establish that the already-published processed eye-gaze inputs or the top-level rerun are unavailable.

The root links are public repository references; root -> data/raw_eyegaze -> src/lab-eyetracking instead names a host-local source. Partial is justified by inspected linkage without converting the no-network restriction into a failed retrieval.

The paper supplies a container recipe and a pinned algorithm. The explicitly linked label generator calls ambient python with an inherited PYTHONPATH and no captured runtime. This concrete second execution boundary supports partial independently of whether container engines themselves must be bundled.

The frozen Git trees track code, manuscript, recipes and configuration, and both root and label components carry pinned gitlinks. Deliberate omissions from an inspection checkout are not changes to the assessed committed object. The positive judgment matches the actual version-control question.

The manifest and Git tree identify annex-backed container layer pointers, including the large image layers, and the linked eye-gaze README explains annex content retrieval. These support use of large-content version control; they do not verify payload availability.

I read both commit objects. The paper run records exit 0, container/image as extra input and img/results_def.tex outputs. The label-generation run records bash and data paths without an environment, and those labels feed the histogram function. Partial correctly reflects the expanded computational scope.

The updated README names required host installations and supplies clone, rerun and manuscript commands. Docker-Makefile implements the corresponding entry points. The old virtualenv route is explicitly labeled old, so the two sections alone do not establish a silent documentation conflict.

The README identifies results-containerized and separately gives the manuscript command; the historical record contains the matching executable numerical/figure command. This establishes an actionable top-level starting point without claiming a new successful execution.

The linked component still documents the Condor route, whose launchers embed an author directory and a specific host interpreter path. The modern compute_all script uses relative data paths. Partial distinguishes the specific legacy defect from intentional container-internal mount paths.

The Docker recipe covers paper analysis and rendering libraries, whereas the label generator inherits its interpreter and environment. The host tool list is useful but not a complete captured orchestration environment. Partial has a concrete component-level basis; dependency freezing should not be confused with simple dependency inclusion.

The README describes tested platforms and Docker format compatibility. Through README datalad-container 1.2.3 -> registered adapter, the supplied adapter explicitly assumes non-root Docker access; the root instructions do not explain it. Linked Condor launchers also inherit host environment variables and an author directory. Partial is supported.

There is a clear top-level list of DataLad, its Containers extension and Docker, plus an explicit guest package list. The algorithm also declares its library dependencies. This criterion asks for a documented requirements list, so incomplete exact runtime capture need not negate this positive separately from must/010 and must/015.

The environment recipe, registration and manifest are committed with the study code. Their presence in version control is established even though the linked label execution has incomplete environment capture.

The introduction commit supplies a runnable build command; subsequent history records an installation-environment correction and an executable OCI conversion with exit 0. This is more than a file introduced once. The duplicate flag matches the identical should/008 wording.

The archive and adapter establish an exact image identity for the paper run: latest is merely a saved tag and execution uses the configuration hash. But met requires the property across the declared object. The same assessment correctly includes label generation under must/006 and must/010; that component has no frozen environment with which others could attempt exact replication. Restricting this item silently to the paper image is inconsistent.

Some current OCI objects use docker-blobs URLs in addition to older docker-layers locations.

The top-level documentation specifies installation sources, clone/rerun and containerized manuscript use; registration invokes the supplied adapter for the archived image. This supports documentation on obtaining and using the paper environment. It does not repair the separate absence of a label-generation environment.

Root and linked component revisions are expressed through Git gitlinks and annex identifiers. The common Git/DataLad graph supports met even though every module need not store all binary payloads in the same backend.

The linked library has a defined installation/test workflow; the paper has a substantial 2023 recomputation and a 2025 compatibility operation. Those are positive testing evidence, but neither establishes regular checking of the complete documented paper instructions. Partial is more accurate than either blanket met or an absence claim based solely on missing root CI.

Raw eye-gaze and derived labels are separate linked datasets, algorithm code is a separate gitlink, and the study uses distinct analysis, image and figure locations. The histogram code reads labels and writes figures under img, preserving the input/output separation relevant to this item.

The 2023 exit-0 record plus docker run --rm is valid historical evidence of a fresh container invocation for numerical results and figures; no new rerun is needed to credit it. However, this command does not build main.pdf, and the explicitly included label workflow is recorded as ambient bash/python. A whole-scope met goes beyond the concrete execution evidence. The same scope is already treated as partial under should/005.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial: credit the recorded fresh-container analysis execution and identify label generation and a recorded fresh manuscript build as uncovered. Do not downgrade the demonstrated paper run to not-checked merely because this review is inspection-only.

The record confirms use of the archived analysis image and a later load/run/format conversion. The conversion payload is exit 0, not re-execution of all figures or manuscript, and the library CI constructs a different environment. Partial is supported; regular exact-environment reconstitution remains unestablished.

The committed archive contains indexed config/layer identities with annex pointers, which is stronger than a registry tag alone. This supports archiving the environment artifact in the research-object structure. Missing frozen payload bytes limit integrity and retrieval checks rather than disproving that architecture.

The same executable build instruction and later tracked environment modifications support this duplicate of must/014. Both original answers are met and explicitly flag the upstream duplication; there is no inconsistency between the pair.

The required eye-gaze data advertise unrestricted access, the manuscript identifies public linked inputs, and the algorithm is openly licensed. The inspected paper code consumes eye-gaze/labels rather than a restricted movie payload. Empty-subject not-applicable is justified; inaccessible source linkage is not itself access restriction.

Root .gitmodules links two data components and the algorithm; the algorithm then links the evaluation inputs. The inspected Git trees supply actual revision pins. This directly satisfies submodule inclusion without making a claim about current remote retrieval.

The root prose explains versioned input inclusion, but the nested label README describes an older Condor procedure and provides no current component/recombination explanation. Thus partial has a documentation-specific basis rather than merely penalizing different pinned algorithm versions.

The offered evidence does not identify a modular boundary that actually causes update breakage. Distinct root and label algorithm pins allow controlled independent histories; updating one need not update the other. The README dependency-drift incident concerns environment reconstruction, not demonstrated failure of the module interfaces. Absence of a compatibility check alone does not establish the specific violation required for partial.
findings.suggested_correction: Identify a concrete cross-module interface/update incompatibility to support partial, or use not-checked for unverified update compatibility. If judging only the design property, explain whether pinned independent modules and stable file interfaces suffice for met; do not treat differing revisions as a defect by themselves.

findings.explanation: Gitlinks supply a versioned composition graph, registration mounts the common project root, and Make targets consume those paths. The run record names the composed inputs and outputs. These are concrete composition mechanisms.

The root offers practical DataLad commands and module metadata for navigation. Partial usefully credits existing tooling while identifying specific downstream navigation gaps.

limitations: Inspection-only review of the assigned anonymized native response, pinned instrument and frozen remodnav-e3c6253bced7 corpus. Manifest SHA256 verified as e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. No peer outputs or other assessments were read.

No network, payload acquisition, container build or scientific execution occurred. Annex data, container layers and omitted binary products cannot be checked for current availability, content integrity or numerical equivalence; absence in this package is not a retrieval failure.
